title: Question about animation
author: Cyber_47_
selftext: So I have come really far with my game project, have done models, story and all but animations are really a nightmare for me. As you know Claude or GPT cant really create great animations, i tried but its mostly bad. I searched for different solutions like video to motion, or text to motion but the ones I used, either didnt work or had terrible results. For example Tripos animation system is really really bad and doesnt fulfill my needs. So my question is how do you do it, and I know there are finished animations on mixamo but I dont mean that. Thanks

comments.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
comments.body: Tell it to set up a tool chain that allows it to screenshot the animations on different poses/frames, then tell Opus 5.5 (if using Claude) to solve the animations as IK even if your rigs don't use IK.  It does VERY well like that.

replies.author: Cyber_47_
replies.body:
bro idk if its the character that im using, the rig or whatever. It worked for an hour with almost all of my daily limit eaten, and the animation still looks like crap. 

https://preview.redd.it/uv8hrduqq2vh1.png?width=1440&format=png&auto=webp&s=338ea52978ba2b1d45d9ca1461ef2a2cc4fd2a81

replies.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
replies.body: Tell it that limbs and fingers are not allowed to intersect dummy props, and to use dummy props in the character rig "_dummy_phone" etc so that it has something to measure against

replies.author: Cyber_47_
replies.body: i mean thats just a part of the problem, its looks off everywhere. What rig do you use? maybe I should change the rig or something

replies.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
replies.body: I edited my comment and added a bit more that might help.  The rig shouldn't matter, just need to help the IK solver as much as you can so AI doesn't need to pretend it knows what's going on

comments.author: Nilo_Team
comments.body:
hey hey- meshy auto-rig fighting you on deformations is super common. for a biped character try gen (or drop a clean T-pose) on nilo.io, hit auto-rig there, then export GLB/FBX into unreal - model settings + LOD first so the mesh isn't a soup. 

weapons as separate gens you attach yourself usually beats baking the grip into one fused mesh. free plan covers a few tests. weapon-hand polish still wants a pass in blender/unreal though - LMK :)

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body: I feel like we're entering the era of "code driven animation" instead of making things from scratch with diffusion models. Setting up the right system you could have Claude talk to different animation software like after effects or it's now ai open source version. But really as long as it's something that can output anything even a web page, it's trivial to ask Claude to change it a frame at a time and output a video.
